sketches.title: Room Tone
sketches.premise: The Host names an ordinary household sound. You and the House each pitch a band name and debut album for it. The Host awards points for how far the pitch travels without losing the sound’s identity; then you call which pitch better matches the sound’s checkable truth.
sketches.criterion: The pitch must preserve the sound’s real source and the specific action that makes it, while treating every invented band or album detail as fair.
sketches.move_shape: Write one headline-style line containing a band name and an album title, both making the sound recognizable without naming it; for a dripping tap: “The Patient Plink — debut album: One Drop at a Time.”
sketches.first_card: A spoon clinking against a mug

sketches.title: Household Hit
sketches.premise: The Host deals a household sound and two plain nouns it suggests. You and the House each turn those nouns into a band name and debut album, then the Host judges the result. Points reward imaginative distance while the sound still holds; afterward, call which pitch better fits the sound’s real cause.
sketches.criterion: The pitch must keep the dealt sound’s source and action intact, and must use both nouns as meaningful parts of the band name or album title.
sketches.move_shape: Write a band name followed by an album title, using both nouns without simply describing the sound; for a zipper and a coat: “The Metal Teeth — debut album: Jacket Weather.”

sketches.title: The Opening Act
sketches.premise: The Host names a household sound and gives its ordinary setting. You and the House each submit a band name and debut album that make the sound feel like a musical act. The Host scores boldness that survives the setting, and you call which pitch gets the sound right.
sketches.criterion: The pitch must remain possible in the given setting and must retain the sound’s real maker, motion, and rough character.
sketches.move_shape: Write one band name and one album title, with no explanation; for a doorbell at the front door: “The Polite Button — debut album: Someone’s Here.”
sketches.first_card: A radiator ticking as it warms

sketches.title: Minor Household
sketches.premise: The Host deals a small household sound plus two everyday nouns. You and the House each name a band and its first album as if the sound had a short, serious career. The Host gives points for a surprising leap that still lands on the sound, then you identify the pitch that preserves the real-world fact.
sketches.criterion: The pitch must make the sound’s source and physical action remain true, while the two nouns must both do useful work rather than sit as decoration.
sketches.move_shape: Write “Band — Album,” using the two nouns in either title; for a key in a lock: “The Tiny Turn — First album: Doorway Business.”

sketches.title: Quiet Label
sketches.premise: The Host gives a household sound and two nouns from its ordinary scene. You and the House each launch a band and debut album with one compact line. The Host rewards the most distinctive pitch that does not contradict the sound, and then you call which line keeps the real clue hidden but intact.
sketches.criterion: The line must fit the sound’s real source, action, and scene without stating the sound’s identity outright, and both nouns must be used as title material.
sketches.move_shape: Submit one line in the form “Band — Album”; for a fridge humming beside a magnet: “The Cold Current — debut album: Stuck to the Noise.”

sketches.title: House Band
sketches.premise: The Host deals a household sound and two nouns, then you and the House each give that sound a band name and debut album. The Host scores how much personality the line gains while its cause remains possible; finally, you call which entry better protects the sound’s real, checkable truth.
sketches.criterion: The pitch must preserve what makes the sound happen and must incorporate both nouns, with invented biography and genre treated as harmless invention.
sketches.move_shape: Write a single “Band — Album” headline; for a pencil tapping on a desk: “The Second Thought — debut album: Wood on Wood.”
sketches.first_card: A washing machine shaking during a spin cycle
